_comment: D-SINK-43..46 (owner, 2026-10-29: pin + classify, not a strict allowlist).
EVERY option base the installed mpv offers, with the class that decides what the
plugin does with a user's mpvArgs token for it and with the user's own mpv.conf.
Read by tests/test_player.py and tests/Model.test.js (both mirrors' MPV_RESERVED
and the trailing pin block must equal what this file says) and by
scripts/check-mpv-options.py, which the gate runs against `mpv --list-options`
and which goes RED on any option this file does not classify: a new mpv option
is a decision, not a default.
`why` is required for every string-shaped option (String, String list,
Key/value list, Object settings list, [file]) and for aliases; flags and numbers
in bulk carry none. An alias takes its target's class. ASCII only.

classes.allowed: a user token passes the filter and lands after the base argv
classes.reserved: a user token is REFUSED (both mirrors' MPV_RESERVED); the user's own mpv.conf is the user's
classes.pinned: re-asserted by the trailing pin block, AFTER the user's tokens, so no token, named profile, plain mpv.conf line or per-file profile can change it; REFUSED in mpvArgs as well, except a key-pinned list (pinKey), whose other keys stay the user's
classes.warned: kept, with the PO-10 footer warning (MPV_HANDOFF / MPV_DISK_WARN)
classes.base: set by the plugin BEFORE the user's tokens; a user token may override it

_comment: D-SINK-43: FFmpeg's own TLS protocol options, as `ffmpeg -hide_banner -h protocol=tls` lists
them (FFmpeg n9.0.1). For an HLS or DASH stream a --demuxer-lavf-o key reaches every one of
them on every segment open. `pinned`: must read "1" when present (DEMUXER_TLS_ON in the
helper; the pin block appends tls_verify=1). `forbidden`: must be absent (DEMUXER_TLS_FORBIDDEN).
`allowed`: neither weakens the peer check. Every pinned or forbidden key must contain one of
`words`, the substrings the token filter refuses (MPV_DEMUXER_TLS_WORDS in both mirrors).
2026-10-29 (lane-p1b, D-SINK-55): the words also hold the two format-context keys in `ffmpegFormat`;
(lane-p1c, D-SINK-62 and D-SINK-64) and its format-list keys and the hls segment demuxer's options.

_comment: D-SINK-55 (2026-10-29): the AVFormatContext keys of a --demuxer-lavf-o map that decide which protocols
libavformat may open below the demuxer -- an HLS segment, a sniffed SDP's rtp. `pinned`: the pin block
appends protocol_whitelist and the helper's read-back requires exactly MPV_PROTOCOL_WHITELIST;
`forbidden`: refused in a token by the same words. Not FFmpeg TLS options, so the mpv option guard does
not list them; tests/test_mpv_options.py holds them to the helper.
2026-10-29 (lane-p1c): D-SINK-62's format_whitelist is pinned the same way (MPV_FORMAT_WHITELIST), and
`removed` (D-SINK-64) is refused in a token AND removed from the map before every load, the read-back
counting it (DEMUXER_FORMAT_FORBIDDEN in the helper).

why.protocol_whitelist: measured: an http(s) stream server answering with an SDP body made the player bind 0.0.0.0:P and P+1; with the pinned list it bound nothing and every admitted scheme played or reached its server
why.protocol_blacklist: a user list of its own would sit beside the pinned whitelist; refused by the same words rather than reasoned about
why.format_whitelist: measured: a stream server answering with an IMF composition playlist, or an ffconcat file naming one, made the player bind 0.0.0.0 through the asset URIs; with the pinned list FFmpeg refused the format at the top level and in every nested context, and every admitted channel kind played
why.format_blacklist: FFmpeg n9.0.1 has no such key; refused by the same words rather than reasoned about
why.seg_format_options: the hls segment demuxer's options, a dictionary FFmpeg reads with its own escapes: format\_whitelist inside it carries no word and replaced the pinned list in the segment's context (measured: with extension_picky=0 an SDP segment bound 0.0.0.0)
